title: TDS vs SDS: Key Differences
excerpt: A TDS is manufacturer technical documentation, while an SDS is the standardized workplace hazard-information document required under OSHA's Hazard Communication framework for covered hazardous chemicals.
content_html:
A Technical Data Sheet (TDS) and a Safety Data Sheet (SDS) can both describe the same product, but they serve different documentation roles.

TDS: technical product information

A TDS commonly summarizes product properties, intended applications, performance characteristics or other manufacturer technical information. Its format can vary.

SDS: standardized hazard information

An SDS follows OSHA's standardized 16-section structure for workplace hazard communication. It contains defined categories of hazard, control and technical information for covered hazardous chemicals.

The level of standardization is different

OSHA specifies SDS section headings and required information. A TDS does not use that OSHA-mandated 16-section structure.

The purpose is different

The TDS is primarily a technical-reference document. The SDS supports hazard communication, worker access to safety information and workplace chemical-safety programs.

Neither automatically replaces the product label

The product label remains the direct source of container-level information, and regulated labels can carry legally enforceable use conditions.

Practical takeaway

Use the TDS for technical product context and the SDS for standardized workplace hazard information. Where both exist, they should refer to the same exact product and current documentation set.
